newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-STRASBOURG OUST MONACO, MEET BORDEAUX IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STRASBOURG OUST MONACO, MEET BORDEAUX IN FINAL.

text.p: Striker David Zitelli scored twice to give Strasbourg a 2-1 win over Monaco on Tuesday and a place in the French League Cup final against Bordeaux.

Bordeaux's Belgian goalkeeper Gilbert Bodard saved three penalties then scored the winning spot-kick as his side beat Montpellier 7-6 in a shoot-out following a 2-2 draw after extra time in the earlier semifinal.

Zitelli, who has scored five goals in the League Cup as well as 16 in the first division championship, put Strasbourg in front when his 45th-minute free kick from the left curled in as the Monaco defence were deceived by a dummy by Olivier Dacourt.
First division leaders Monaco, who started with a second string line-up, brought on heavy duty forwards Anderson and Victor Ikpeba 10 minutes into the second half and were level on the hour.
Brazilian striker Anderson equalised with a volley after his header following a cross from the left by Ikpeba was blocked by a Strasbourg defender.
Zitelli tapped in the winner from a tight angle on the left of the box nine minutes later after Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez could only turn aside a shot from the right by Pascal Nouma.
Strasbourg missed two clear chances to go further ahead from counter-attacks as Monaco pressed for an equaliser and Nigeria's Ikpeba had a shot blocked on the line in the dying minutes.
The final, with the winners qualifying for the UEFA Cup next season, will be played in Paris on April 12.
At Bordeaux, Bodard made successive stops as the first three penalties in the shoot-out were all saved.
He then pounced on Montpellier's ninth penalty by Polish striker Roman Kosecki before beating his opposite number Philippe Flucklinger to put Bordeaux through.

Captain Patrick Colleter, who won the League Cup with Paris St Germain when it was first played two seasons ago, could have settled the issue sooner for Bordeaux. But he blasted his side's fifth penalty against the crossbar.
It was Bordeaux's second successive win on penalties in the competition after beating Caen at home in the quarter-finals.

Midfielder Stephane Ziani put Bordeaux in front four minutes into the second half of normal time when he weaved past two defenders and surprised Flucklinger with a low shot which the goalkeeper got an arm to but could not stop.
Montpellier equalised through Ivory Coast striker Ibrahim Bakayoko, whose low shot, half-parried by Bodard, trickled over the line just before it could be cleared by defender Bernard Lambourde.
The home side went ahead again in the sixth minute of extra time when striker Kaba Diawara was unchalleneged as he headed home a cross from the right by substitute Francois Grenet.
But Bordeaux, whose last trophies were the championship and French Cup double in 1987, gave away a second equaliser 11 minutes from the end.
The defence stood back for Laurent Robert's left-footed free kick from the right and Bodard was too late to reach the ball before it curled into the net at the far post.
